'''Lorena Céspedes Fernández''' (born 18 July 1973) is a [[Chileans|Chilean]] physics teacher and independent politician.<ref name="BCN">{{cite web |url=https://www.bcn.cl/historiapolitica/convencionales_constituyentes/ficha/Lorena_Céspedes_Fernández |title=Lorena Céspedes Fernández |website=Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional de Chile |language=es |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref> She served as a member of the [[Constitutional Convention (Chile)|Constitutional Convention]], representing the 23rd electoral district of the [[Araucanía Region]].

She served as deputy vice president of the Convention between 29 July 2021 and 6 January 2022 and acted as coordinator of the Committee on Constitutional Principles, Democracy, Nationality, and Citizenship.<ref name="BCN"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pauta.cl/politica/vicepresidencia-transversal-lorena-cespedes-y-dialogo-entre-personas|title=Diálogo "entre personas, más que entre bancadas": la vicepresidencia transversal de Lorena Céspedes|publisher=[[Radio Pauta]]|date=29 July 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Céspedes Fernández was born on 18 July 1973.<ref name="BCN"/> She is the daughter of Filadelfo Omar Céspedes Galleguillos and Silvia Graciela Fernández Opazo. She is married to Guillermo Venegas Middleton.<ref name="BCN"/>

She completed her secondary education at Colegio Las Condes.<ref name="BCN"/> She later studied physics and pedagogy at the [[University of Chile]], obtaining a degree in Physics and a teaching qualification.<ref name="BCN"/>

Since 1999, she has worked as a teacher in various institutions, promoting the development of science and technology in the Araucanía Region through teaching, educational events, and science-oriented initiatives.<ref name="BCN"/>

==Political career==
Céspedes Fernández is an independent politician and a member of the External Advisory Council of the Center for Public Policy at the [[Pontifical Catholic University of Chile]].<ref name="BCN"/> In 2018, she was one of the five finalists of the [[Global Teacher Prize]] Chile.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://araucania.mineduc.cl/2018/08/23/seremi-de-educacion-reconoce-a-profesora-semifinalista-del-global-teacher-prize/ |title=Seremi de Educación reconoce a profesora semifinalista del Global Teacher Prize |publisher=Ministerio de Educación – Región de La Araucanía |date=23 August 2018 |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref>

In the elections held on 15–16 May 2021, she ran as an independent candidate for the 23rd electoral district of the Araucanía Region as part of the Independents for a New Constitution electoral pact, receiving 5,546 votes (3.4% of the valid votes).<ref name="BCN"/>

On 29 July 2021, she was confirmed as deputy vice president of the Constitutional Convention’s governing board, a position she held until 6 January 2022.<ref name="BCN"/>
